Are you a senior software developer who views LLMs not as a magic fix, but as components of a larger, complex system? Do you want to move past superficial prompt engineering to design deep, asynchronous workflows that make AI agents reliably useful for real-world developers and take ownership of technical decisions in a culture that treats engineering as a craft?
About JetBrains
We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

AI coding agents are shifting how software is built, but making them truly effective within an IDE requires solving difficult orchestration and integration problems. Within the Air ADE Agents & Integrations team, our goal is to take existing agents – such as Claude Code, Gemini, and Junie – and integrate them deeply into the Air ecosystem across desktop, web, and cloud surfaces.
This is a backend-oriented engineering role where you will influence the core business logic that connects AI agent capabilities with everyday developer workflows. Rather than focusing solely on LLM training, you will solve problems around context management, tool orchestration, and error recovery.

You will work closely with our core product engineers and specialized AI/ML teams to translate open-ended developer interactions into highly responsive, concurrent technical architectures. You will have full ownership over how these systems are built, directly impacting how millions of developers interact with AI tools.

Design, implement, and develop the core product and business logic for agent-based developer workflows in Air.
Build deep integrations between Air product surfaces, external APIs, local CLIs, and AI coding agents.
Improve the end-to-end user experience for agents, covering setup, context handling, task execution, and failure recovery.
Write highly concurrent and asynchronous logic to manage multi-step agent interactions reliably.
Use AI agents and assistants in your daily development work to analyze their limitations and improve our workflows from firsthand experience.
Write clean, maintainable code, lead technical design discussions, and participate in peer code reviews.
Partner with distributed product and ML engineering teams to break down complex architectural problems.

An engineering mindset that prioritizes long-term system stability and clean architecture over quick patches.
The autonomy to drive technical decisions and responsibility for the outcome.
A collaborative approach to problem-solving, welcoming direct feedback and technical debate.
Curiosity about how AI tools fail in practice and a desire to build systems that gracefully handle those failures.
A strong focus on the developer experience, understanding what makes an integration feel seamless or disruptive.
What you’ll need
Comprehensive experience in professional software development, demonstrating the technical maturity required for senior engineering problems.
Strong programming skills in at least one modern backend language, with the readiness to work primarily in Kotlin.
A deep practical understanding of concurrent and asynchronous programming, including coroutines, threads, async I/O, and synchronization primitives.
A proven track record of building and shipping application workflows, third-party integrations, or service-backed logic.
Hands-on experience working with AI-assisted development tools, alongside an understanding of task orchestration, tool usage, and prompt context management.
A solid understanding of software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, debugging, observability, and test-driven development.
Fluency in written and spoken English for day-to-day technical collaboration across distributed teams.
What success looks like
Success in this role means building robust, low-latency integration pipelines that make AI agents feel like a natural extension of the Air environment. You will earn the trust of the team by creating reliable, asynchronous workflows that handle unpredictable LLM behaviors without compromising IDE performance. You win when you move past inherited frameworks to establish internal standards for agent tooling, leaving the codebase cleaner, faster, and more maintainable than you found it.

You are someone who takes full ownership of your work and thrives on delivering solutions. If there’s a problem in our system, no matter where the root cause lies, you pursue it until it’s resolved — ensuring our customers experience a seamless service.

What does ServiceTrade do?
ServiceTrade is a best-in-class field service management platform that helps commercial fire protection and mechanical service contractors build efficient and growing businesses. With more than a decade of innovation and 1500 customers, ServiceTrade streamlines operations from the field to the office, boosts technician productivity, and enhances the end-customer experience.
Ok, so why should I care about that?
Our customers do essential work — often behind the scenes — and our software helps them do it better. They’re smart, hardworking people, and we take pride in helping them grow their businesses, earn more revenue, employ more skilled workers, and deliver greater value to their own customers. When you work at ServiceTrade , your impact extends beyond our walls, supporting communities and markets you might never have thought about — and making work that truly matters every day.
What kind of working environment do you have?
We’re a growing business focused on building with intention and operating with purpose. You’ll have meaningful responsibility and the trust to do your best work from the start. We encourage calculated risks and bold experimentation, while providing opportunities to learn, grow, and turn today’s lessons into tomorrow’s breakthroughs—all in service of big ambitions and real customer impact.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

The Safeguards ML Inference Path team designs, builds, and operates the production infrastructure that powers Claude's ML based safety systems. We collaborate closely with safety researchers and inference engineers to bring new classifiers and novel classes of ML defenses to production.

We own the research → production transfer of new safety technologies that is on the critical path for every Claude model launch. And we build for scale: serving thousands of ML classifiers, for all requests on the token generation path, and for every platform Claude runs on -- 1P, Bedrock, Vertex, and beyond.
We’re growing the team and looking for engineers who have deep expertise in productionizing ML systems. You'll work at the intersection of machine learning, large-scale distributed systems, and AI safety, developing the platforms and tools that enable our safeguards to operate reliably at scale. And your tooling and infrastructure will be used for every model launch, which are becoming more complex, and more frequent.

Design and build scalable ML infrastructure to support real-time safety deployments across our classifier and model ecosystem
Build monitoring and observability tools to track classifier performance, data quality, and system health for safety-critical applications
Collaborate with research teams to productionize safety research, translating experimental safety techniques into robust, scalable systems
Optimize inference latency and throughput for real-time safety evaluations while maintaining high reliability standards
Implement automated testing, deployment, and rollback systems for ML models in production safety applications
Partner with Safeguards, Security, and Alignment teams to understand requirements and deliver infrastructure that meets safety and production needs
Contribute to the development of internal tools and frameworks that accelerate safety research and deployment

Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work.

We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains.

Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.
How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles.

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

s.h: So, what's the role all about?

You'll architect and deliver production-ready conversational AI agents that sit at the core of the business and directly fuel company growth.
These are live, scalable agentic AI systems, not experiments or proof-of-concepts, operating across sectors like financial services, healthcare, and commerce.
You'll have full ownership of the entire AI agent lifecycle, steering projects from early pilot through launch and ongoing refinement.
You'll collaborate directly with decision-makers at the world’s leading enterprises to tackle their highest-priority challenges with agentic AI.
The patterns and problems you encounter in the field will feed directly into the evolution of the platform, tools, and product roadmap.
How will you make an impact?
Develop agentic systems (agents) for large-scale companies that measurably outperform human operators in areas like retention and churn reduction.
Build agents that handle nuanced, integrated customer interactions, across a range of CX transforming use cases.
Design reusable agent frameworks adapted to the specific demands of different industries.
Drive design partnerships around new product directions, including agent architectures, self-service features, and generative development workflows.
Push the boundaries with emerging voice models and pioneer their integration into enterprise-grade deployments.
Set the standard for how AI agents are constructed, evaluated, and improved in live production settings.
Have you got what it takes?
Hands-on experience building and operating end-to-end production systems at scale.
With a natural builder's mentality with high personal agency, you default to finding solutions and shipping them.
Startup founder or early engineer experience is highly valued, you understand the tradeoffs between speed, quality, and ownership.
Proven technical problem-solving ability, particularly in rapidly shifting, loosely defined environments.
Experience developing or operating AI/LLM-powered systems in production is a major plus.
Working knowledge of the current AI agent toolkit: evaluation frameworks, orchestration tooling, RAG pipelines, and prompt engineering.
Familiarity with React, TypeScript, and/or Go is an advantage.
At ease working face-to-face with customers to unpack their problems and deliver practical solutions.
Prior experience in customer-facing or externally-led technical roles is a plus.
A clear, direct communicator who can be equally persuasive with engineers and executives.
Comfortable operating in ambiguity and making forward progress without waiting for complete clarity.
Able to balance competing priorities and drive alignment across technical and business teams.
What's in it for you?
Build AI agents that run in production at meaningful scale, not slideware or research exercises.
Work shoulder-to-shoulder with leaders at globally recognized enterprises and high-growth startups.
Directly influence the direction of NiCE's AI agent platform through the real problems you solve.
Operate with genuine autonomy and end-to-end ownership across the agent lifecycle.
Work at the cutting edge of AI agent development with access to the latest models, infrastructure, and research.

When the Tarr Steps, a footbridge assembled of heavy stones in Exmoor National Park in England, washed away in a flood in 1942, the Royal Engineers rebuilt it. Then it washed away again in 1952. So the Royal Engineers heaved in more stones: on and on, like a Sisyphean lesson in absurdity.
Of course, they do this because the Tarr Steps are a historical monument, believed to be built during the Bronze Age. Modern bridge building looks a lot different and generally requires less upkeep. While we appreciate the charm of ancient things, Mercury is engineering the future of banking*.

"Quaint" and "archaic" are not values we seek in our systems. Rebooting a tumbling server and hoping a flood of requests doesn't wash it away can be an emergency tactic, but we actively seek out durable solutions over monotonous ops work. You'll bring this ethos and teach others how to live it too.
Up to this point, the Stability team at Mercury has primarily built platform-level constructs that product teams adopt. However, those teams are asking for us to work more closely with them to mature their implementations and practices. We are creating an SRE team that will rotate through product teams. You will understand the team's domain, identify opportunities for improvements in reliability/observability/performance/preparedness and create self-reinforcing, virtuous cycles.

s.h: As part of this role, you will
s.t:
Embed with product teams, helping them improve their operational maturity by setting up and refining practices around on-call, monitoring, alerting, and run books
Run regular game day exercises with product teams, helping them feel more prepared to investigate and quickly remediate incidents
Jump into application code written in Haskell & TypeScript and implement reliability techniques such as retries, better error handling, better logging, circuit breaking, etc
Steer SLOs towards meaningful customer outcomes that product teams are accountable for. Those SLOs become a strong signal for whether the product is working as intended
Champion reliability practices through design document and code reviews

s.h: What does the team work on?
s.t:
The Roku Enterprise Engineering team is at the forefront of building a robust, integrated, and scalable platform that powers critical business processes across the organisation.

As a cornerstone of Roku's corporate strategy, this team is instrumental in automating workflows across all Business Systems, including Supply Chain, Finance, Sales Operations, and Human Resources.

By challenging traditional approaches to workflow automation, the team leverages cutting-edge engineering practices and API-driven design to streamline internal processes, boost efficiency, and deliver innovative solutions.

The team's expertise spans a wide range of technologies, including Java and Python-based MicroServices, AWS/GCP cloud backend systems, Big Data technologies like Hive and Spark, and modern web applications.

With a globally distributed presence across the US, India, and Europe, the team thrives on collaboration, bringing together diverse perspectives to solve complex challenges.

At the heart of their success is a shared commitment to technical excellence, creativity, a strong sense of ownership, and a collaborative spirit that drives impactful results for Roku's business operations.

Roku is seeking a Senior Software Engineer to join the Enterprise Engineering team, focused on designing, building, and deploying scalable web applications and services that power critical business processes.

In this role, you will serve as a platform services developer, building innovative solutions using modern software frameworks and paradigms across a multi-tier, distributed architecture. You will drive architecture discussions, take ownership of new projects, and deliver high-quality software within tight timelines.

You will partner closely with security, compliance, and cross-functional teams to ensure applications meet audit, security, and compliance requirements. This role requires a self-driven problem solver with a strong background in building large-scale software platforms, microservices, and cloud-based systems.

You will also contribute to the continual improvement of engineering tools, cloud-based technologies, and development processes, playing an integral role in shaping the team's technical direction.
How will I use AI at Roku?
At Roku, AI agents do most of the keystroke-level coding. Engineers act as the technical leads for those agents — setting architecture, reviewing output, and ensuring everything meets Roku's quality bar.

If you've already shipped features where an AI agent wrote the initial code and you steered it to production, or you've built fluency across the agentic engineering toolchain — coding harnesses like Claude Code or Cursor, MCP servers, custom skills, or agent frameworks.

And you can describe a clear, repeatable workflow: how you prompt, how you scope tasks, how you drive an agent, verify its output, and ramp on an unfamiliar codebase with an agent helping you.
At Roku, we're embracing AI as a powerful tool to amplify human creativity, accelerate innovation, and deliver better results across the company. You already have experience using AI tools — or you're excited to learn how — to enhance your work, make smarter decisions, and collaborate more effectively. Whether you're in engineering, marketing, finance, HR, or any other team, AI will be part of how you work here. We want to talk to you.

Meet Arago and the Aragonians
Arago is an AI and computer hardware company whose mission is to drive the course of history forward. We do so by accelerating breakthroughs at the intersection of AI and semiconductors.
Founded in 2024 by AI researchers and physicists with deep expertise in photonics, electronics, software, mathematics, and machine learning, Arago brings together a lean team of engineers and scientists from the world’s top companies and research labs.
Composed of nine nationalities and operating from hubs in France, North America, and Israel, we believe in great science and fast achievements. Our work is guided by these core principles:
Do great things: we deliver work we’re proud to sign our name to.
High velocity: speed matters. We move quickly, one step at a time.
One unit: we’re all in this together, with relationships grounded in trust, respect, and camaraderie.
Arago is backed by executives from Apple, Arm, Nvidia, Microsoft, and Hugging Face, as well as prominent US and European deeptech venture firms and exited founders.

As a Performance Software Engineer, you will be instrumental in building the core computation software that runs on Arago’s custom AI accelerators. Your work will bridge the gap between host systems and proprietary hardware, encompassing everything from a custom on-board kernels to the sophisticated tooling required for real-time debugging.

You will be a key player in chip bring-up and the long-term development of high-performance computation primitives and kernels, ensuring our architecture operates with maximum efficiency and deterministic performance.

Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
Strong experience in low-level systems programming using C/C++ and assembly, with excellent understanding of how compiled software maps to machine instructions and hardware behavior.
Deep familiarity with bare-metal development, including startup code, linker scripts, memory layout, MMIO, interrupts/exceptions, timers, synchronization, and direct peripheral access.
Strong understanding of computer architecture, including pipelines, caches, memory hierarchies, virtual/physical addressing, atomics, DMA, and performance implications of different access patterns.
Hands-on experience with RISC-V and/or ARM architectures, instruction sets, calling conventions, ABI concepts, and architecture-specific intrinsics.
Experience debugging hardware/software interactions using tools such as GDB, JTAG, trace/debug interfaces, simulators, emulators, or FPGA platforms.
Ability to read hardware specifications, register descriptions, and RTL-level documentation and translate them into robust software implementations.
Strong performance-analysis and optimization skills, including profiling, disassembly inspection, compiler optimization behavior, and hand-tuned assembly where appropriate.
Language: English at a proficient level. French is a plus.

Develop and optimize low-level software primitives in C/C++, assembly, and architecture-specific intrinsics, primarily for RISC-V and ARM platforms.
Implement performance-critical kernels, runtime components, hardware abstraction layers, drivers, and firmware operating in bare-metal or highly constrained environments.
Work closely with hardware architects and RTL/design teams to define and validate hardware-software interfaces, memory maps, register interfaces, interrupts, synchronization mechanisms, and boot flows.
Analyze and optimize software for latency, throughput, memory footprint, instruction count, and efficient use of processor and accelerator features.
Bring up and debug software on simulation, emulation, FPGA, and silicon platforms, including low-level hardware/software integration issues.
Develop validation tests, benchmarks, and diagnostic tools for new processor, DSP, accelerator, and SoC functionality.
Contribute to architecture decisions around ISA extensions, compiler intrinsics, memory hierarchy, DMA, cache/coherency behavior, and software-visible hardware features.

## Description de l'entreprise ##
**Swiss Medical Network** est l'un des groupes de cliniques privées les plus importants de Suisse. Il s'est fixé pour objectif d'offrir des soins médicaux de premier ordre à ses patients suisses et étrangers.

Swiss Medical Network convainc par la haute qualité de ses prestations, un environnement de travail agréable et une équipe de direction expérimentée à l'esprit entrepreneurial. Le réseau exploite actuellement 21 cliniques et hôpitaux dans toute la Suisse et est présent dans les trois principales régions linguistiques.
## Description du poste ##
En tant que **Fullstack Developer (AI & Digital Health)**, vous jouez un rôle moteur dans la transformation numérique de nos cliniques. Vous concevez et développez des solutions logicielles innovantes assistées par l'IA, qui améliorent le parcours du patient tout en soulageant le personnel médical. Vous agissez comme un pont technique entre les exigences médicales et les technologies de pointe, garantissant que nos applications de santé numériques sont sécurisées, évolutives et conviviales.

**Votre domaine d'activité**
* **Développement & Architecture de solutions :** Conception et implémentation d'applications web Fullstack évolutives (Frontend & Backend) pour un usage clinique et administratif.
* **Intégration de l'IA :** Développement et intégration de modèles d'apprentissage automatique (Machine Learning), de LLM (Large Language Models) et de services d'IA déterministes (explainable AI) dans des applications existantes et nouvelles pour soutenir les processus diagnostiques ou administratifs.
* **Données & Interfaces :** Connexion des applications aux systèmes primaires cliniques (KIS/HIS/DPI) en utilisant des standards d'interopérabilité modernes (ex. FHIR, HL7) et garantie d'un échange de données fluide.
* **Security by Design :** Garantie des standards de sécurité les plus élevés et de la conformité à la protection des données (LPD/RGPD) lors du traitement des données sensibles des patients, en étroite coordination avec le délégué à la protection des données.
* **DevOps & Cloud :** Mise en place et maintenance de pipelines CI/CD ainsi que gestion de l'infrastructure Cloud pour l'exploitation des solutions d'IA.
* **Prototyping :** Développement rapide de preuves de concept (PoC) pour évaluer le potentiel des nouvelles technologies d'IA pour le quotidien clinique et les rendre tangibles.
* **Collaboration :** Étroite coopération avec les Data Scientists, les médecins et le personnel soignant afin de créer des solutions centrées sur l'utilisateur ("User Centricity").
**Votre profil**
* **Formation :** Diplôme universitaire en informatique, ingénierie logicielle ou qualification comparable avec un fort accent sur les technologies web modernes.
* **Compétences en développement :** Expérience approfondie dans les frameworks Backend (ex. Python, Node.js, Java) et Frontend (ex. React, Angular, Vue.js) modernes, idéalement sur la Google Cloud Platform (BigQuery, Looker). Des connaissances en Python sont privilégiées en raison de l'orientation IA.
* **Expertise en IA :** Expérience pratique dans l'intégration de composants IA/ML (ex. API OpenAI, LangChain, Hugging Face, TensorFlow) dans des environnements logiciels productifs.
* **Secteur de la santé :** Une expérience avec les normes du secteur de la santé (FHIR, HL7, DICOM) est un avantage, mais pas obligatoire si vous êtes prêt à vous y former. Une expérience avec le "Software as Medical Device" et les processus de certification correspondants constitue un atout majeur.
* **Méthode de travail :** Un mode de travail autonome, agile (Scrum/Kanban) et orienté solutions. Vous avez une mentalité "Can-Do" et prenez plaisir à résoudre des problèmes complexes par le code.
* **Personnalité :** Esprit d'innovation couplé à une conscience de la qualité. Vous savez rendre des sujets techniques compréhensibles pour des interlocuteurs non techniques.
* **Langues :** De langue maternelle allemande avec un niveau courant/négociation en français (ou inversement) ; de bonnes connaissances en anglais sont requises pour la collaboration au sein de nos équipes linguistiques régionales.
* **Tech-Stack :** Des connaissances en technologies de conteneurisation (Docker, Kubernetes), plateformes Cloud (Azure/GCP) et gestion de versions (Git) sont prérequis.
## Informations supplémentaires ##
**Notre offre**
* **Innovation :** Nous vous offrons la possibilité de travailler à la pointe de l'innovation médicale et de développer des solutions d'IA qui apportent une véritable plus-value à la vie des patients.
* **Création :** Vous bénéficiez d'une grande marge de manœuvre technique dans un environnement dynamique qui favorise les circuits de décision courts et la pensée entrepreneuriale.
* **Environnement :** Un climat de travail inspirant au sein d'une équipe interdisciplinaire composée de médecins et de spécialistes IT, un package salarial attractif ainsi que des prestations sociales progressistes vous attendent.
* **Développement :** Réjouissez-vous de projets passionnants avec les dernières technologies et une grande responsabilité personnelle au sein d'un groupe de cliniques en pleine croissance.
**Date d'entrée** De suite ou à convenir
**Lieu de travail** Zurich, Bâle, Soleure, Zofingue, Fribourg, Sion, Genolier ou Genève (missions / projets dans toute la Suisse). Télétravail possible.

💼 Job Title: Principal Software Engineer
📍 Location: Fully remote within Europe (CET ±2 hours)
⏳ Job Type: Full-time
⭐️ Reports to: Director of Engineering

We are looking for a deeply hands-on Principal Software Engineer to be the most senior technical individual contributor at Hi Rasmus . Reporting to our Director of Engineering, this is a role on our Principal track, a craft career path that sits alongside the management track rather than beneath it.
Where a Lead Software Engineer is the strongest technical contributor within one outcome team, the Principal Software Engineer works across all of them. You will help shape and evolve our platform architecture, strengthen shared technical practices, mentor Senior and Lead Engineers, and take on complex challenges that span teams or domains.
This is not an advisory role. You will work alongside teams in the code, helping solve difficult problems and piloting new tools, patterns, and practices through real work. Your goal is not to become a permanent escalation point, but to leave teams more capable of making strong technical decisions independently.
You lead through technical judgement, architecture, code review, collaboration and example rather than through reporting lines. Software Engineers sit in the outcome teams and report to their Lead Engineer.

You will provide technical guidance and mentorship across teams, while people leadership, performance management, staffing and overall Engineering accountability remain with Lead Engineers and the Director of Engineering. As we scale, we are relying increasingly on AI and automation to improve engineering leverage.

Working in partnership with the Director of Engineering and CTO, you will help translate our company and Engineering direction into sound architecture, modern technical practices, and durable internal capability.

Work alongside outcome teams to solve complex technical problems, particularly those spanning systems, teams, or domains.
Pilot new tools, patterns, and practices through real production work before supporting broader adoption.
Facilitate the architecture forum, bringing Product and other stakeholders into decisions early and establishing a clear process for documenting, communicating, and revisiting those decisions.
Partner with the Director of Engineering, CTO, and Lead Engineers to guide the evolution of our web and mobile platform across Vue 3, Quasar, Capacitor, Node.js, Firebase, Firestore, and Google Cloud Platform.
Evaluate and recommend tooling and framework decisions, including build, buy, adopt, or retire recommendations grounded in real evidence and business needs.
Take on the complex, cross-cutting problems that span teams or that no single team can own, and land them in production.
Establish shared technical standards across code quality, testing, APIs, data modelling, documentation, and system design, building adoption through practical value, review, and example.
Surface technical debt, performance, scalability, and system-health risks early, and partner with Engineering leadership to prioritize the right investments.
Strengthen internal ownership of critical systems, architectural decisions, deployment paths, and operational knowledge through clear documentation, knowledge-sharing, and hands-on collaboration.
Build alignment across teams through the Lead Engineers guild while preserving the ownership and autonomy of individual outcome teams.
Advance responsible AI-assisted development practices and evaluate their impact on quality, speed, reliability, privacy, and security. Help scale what works and thoughtfully retire practices that no longer serve us.
Identify technical risk, performance, and scalability problems before they are urgent, and lead the work to remove them.
Mentor Senior and Lead Engineers through pairing, design review, technical feedback, and shared problem-solving.
Contribute to the engineering career ladder and to levelling and calibration, and act as the technical assessor in engineering hiring, with decisions owned by Lead Engineers and the Director of Engineering.
Partner with the Principal QA Engineer, Product, and DevOps so that quality, testability, and operability are designed in rather than added later.
Contribute to compliance and audit readiness by helping make sure our technical practices hold up to external scrutiny in a regulated healthcare context.

s.h: 🌱 What Success Looks LikeWithin your first 6–12 months
s.t:
Teams are using a shared, practical architecture decision process, with important decisions clearly documented and understood.
Ownership of critical domains and systems is clearer, and the highest-priority cross-team technical risks and debt have actionable plans.
AI-assisted development practices are producing measurable improvements without compromising quality, privacy, security, or reliability.
Senior and Lead Engineers are more confident making complex technical decisions, with fewer issues requiring escalation.
Critical platform and operational knowledge is increasingly shared, documented, and owned internally.

Extensive experience as a Senior, Lead, or Principal Software Engineer, with a track record of delivering complex, production-grade systems.
Deep technical capability that remains current. You can step into a difficult problem, contribute meaningfully in the code, and help carry the solution into production.
Deep proficiency in Vue 3 and Node.js, with strong full-stack understanding.
Strong, practical experience with Domain-Driven Design. You can identify bounded contexts within a complex domain, model them thoughtfully, and protect those boundaries under delivery pressure. Experience applying tactical DDD in code is essential.

Investigate customer-reported and production data issues, perform root cause analysis, and drive timely resolution.

Work with real-time data streaming technologies such as Kafka and Flink.
Implement software engineering best practices including CI/CD, source control, automated testing, and deployments.
Identify opportunities for automation and improve operational efficiency through reusable frameworks and utilities.
Leverage Generative AI and Agentic AI capabilities to enhance data engineering workflows, troubleshooting, and productivity.
Contribute to the scalability, reliability, monitoring, and performance optimization of data platforms.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.
8 to 12 years of experience in Data Engineering.
Strong hands-on experience with Snowflake. This is a critical requirement for the role.
Expertise in SQL, ETL/ELT processes, Data Warehousing, Data Modeling, and Data Lake concepts.
Strong hands-on experience with AWS services including S3, IAM, EC2, Lambda, CloudWatch, and SQS/SNS.
Experience integrating Snowflake with AWS-based data ecosystems and Data Lakes.
Experience working with large-scale data platforms and complex datasets.

Exposure to Generative AI and Agentic AI concepts and practical applications.
Experience with Snowflake Cortex or similar AI-enabled data platforms.
Demonstrated experience implementing automation solutions to improve engineering productivity and operational efficiency.

Strong customer-centric problem-solving capabilities.
Ability to trace and analyze data across multiple systems and layers.
Experience building reusable frameworks, utilities, and engineering accelerators.
Strong ownership mindset with a focus on continuous improvement and innovation.

We are seeking a hands-on Principal Software Engineer to build PingOne Privilege, our cloud-native Zero Trust privileged access platform, and the AI security capabilities that protect how enterprises adopt agentic AI. This is a coding role — you will design, ship, and own production systems alongside the rest of the team.

Build the Platform: Design and ship core services for PingOne Privilege, our cloud-native platform in Go — just-in-time access, credential-less authentication, and Zero Trust access to multi-cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP) and on-prem resources.
Agentic AI Security: Build our AI security capabilities hands-on — MCP gateways, AI agent identity and governance, and real-time guardrails that detect and block prompt injection and data exfiltration.
Distributed Systems: Develop highly available, multi-region services on Kubernetes with durable workflow orchestration and distributed data stores, and own them through design, implementation, and production.
Identity & Access Protocols: Implement deep integrations with identity protocols (OAuth2/OIDC, SAML, SCIM, certificate-based auth) and build secure proxy and gateway layers for SSH, RDP, Kubernetes, databases, and web applications.
Technical Leadership: Raise the bar through code reviews and design reviews, mentor engineers by working alongside them, and set the example for high-quality, secure, maintainable code.

Experience: 10+ years of hands-on software engineering experience, with 4+ years at a Principal or Staff level building large-scale security or identity products — as an individual contributor who writes and ships production code daily.
Security & Identity Expertise: Deep working knowledge of IAM/PAM — privileged access, secrets and key management, session brokering, least-privilege and Zero Trust architectures — with hands-on depth in OAuth2/OIDC and PKI.
Tech Stack: Expert-level proficiency in Go (or strong systems-language background with willingness to work in Go), Cloud Native technologies (AWS/Azure/GCP, Kubernetes), and distributed data stores (Cassandra or similar NoSQL); experience with workflow engines (e.g., Temporal) a plus.
AI Systems (preferred): Experience building or securing LLM-based systems — agent frameworks, MCP, model-based threat detection, or AI guardrails.
Leadership: Influence through code and design, not title — proven ability to drive cross-team technical decisions while staying in the critical path of delivery.
Education: BS/MS in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.
